recipes.name: Scalloped Red Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of broccoli soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of celery soup

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter a large baking dish.
Wash and peel potatoes so that only some of the peel remains on the potatoes; cut into 1/8 inch slices.
Arrange potatoes in the prepared dish.

Melt butter in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook onion and garlic in melted butter until soft and translucent, 7 to 10 minutes; stir in broccoli soup, celery soup, milk, salt, pepper, and about ½  of the Cheddar cheese; cook until cheese has melted.
Pour cheese mixture over potatoes; top with remaining Cheddar cheese. Cover with aluminum foil or a lid.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes. Remove the cover and cook until the cheese begins to brown, about 10 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Scalloped Red Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These scalloped red potatoes are total comfort food thanks to the combination of tender sliced potatoes in a rich and creamy Cheddar cheese sauce.

review.reviewBody: I followed the recipe exactly except subsituting cream of mushroom for cream of broccoli. I did what other reviews said - take foil off and bake for another 10-20 minutes. This was AMAZING. I'll probably never buy boxed scalloped potatoes again. Actually, I know I won't. Sooooo good.

These scalloped potatoes were quite delish!! I did however, modify the recipe somewhat. I used 8 cups of extremely thin sliced red potatoes, 1-medium yellow onion diced, and 1 medium red onion diced, 3 large cloves of garlic minced, 1/2 cup of 2% milk, 1/2 cup of half-n-half cream, added 1/2 teaspoon of salt, plus 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper. Only needed to saute' the onions for 3 minutes, then saute'd the garlic for just 1 minute. By mistake I only used 2 cups of the shredded sharp cheddar cheese, which my husband and I thought that was plenty of cheese. I also mixed together, the sliced potatoes and the soup/cheese combination, before adding it to the buttered pan. I like how that help to coat the potatoes nicely. Baked the taters for 1 hour and 25 minutes, and after removing the foil, I continued to bake the potatoes for another 10 minutes. Then let the taters set ontop the stove for 15 minutes, so they'd absorb the sauce in the pan, and sprinkled the top with some dried parsley before serving. I also wanted to add... the next time I do make these potatoes, I'll most likely substitute the cream of broccoli soup for another creamed soup. It's just a preference on my part. What a nice side dish to serve with our Sunday dinner. Thank you metzstar for sharing your recipe!!

I actually sautéed the potatoes with the onion and garlic then added the other ingredients and cooked for about 20 minutes in the stovetop because my oven was "taken." I cooked for 20-30 minutes in the oven. The only substitution I made was only 1 jar of cream of mushroom soup. I added some fresh rosemary and chives from the garden just because.

We did a smaller batch, just used one can of soup and about 3/4 cup milk...making the sauce on the stovetop is what makes this recipe so special! Cooking the potatoes in the rich creamy sauce for the full hour gave the perfect texture! Excellent comfort food! On the top of our list!!!

Made tonight. I'm not one for garlic and pepper. Skipped. 13 X 9 added ham. ONE CAN OF SOUP TOO MANY IN RECIPE !!!! Maybe cut milk to 1/2 c. Boiled over and was more like soupy stew. Otherwise good. Will make again with 1 can of soup.

Good base recipe for a rich and creamy potato! I added chilli flakes and thyme to the sauce to add an extra kick and mixed mushrooms and smoked ham into the potato to make it a full meal. I found it took double the suggested time to cook but that may be because of the extra volume added by the other ingredients.

This was sooo good! 
I changed the recipe a little, due to time constraints and availability of ingredients. 
Added diced Bell pepper, and used only 1 can of cream of mushroom soup, baked in a 9x9 glass dish. 
I also gave the potatoes a head start by steaming them in the microwave for about 4 minutes prior to placing them in the casserole dish. 
Total cook time was about 35 minutes. These were so easy and delicious, would definitely make again!!

All of the stellar reviews for this weren't exaggerating! It was fantastic, according to both the wife and me!!! I followed the recipe exactly, with the exception of not buttering the dish first, but only because I forgot before layering in the potatoes. As it turns out, there was no need! Oh yes, I did use everyone else's "adapted directions" and extended the uncovered baking time to 20 or 25 minutes. So perfect! Also, it's just the two of us, so I actually split the recipe into two smaller pyrex dishes and put one in the freezer (pre-baking). We'll see how that one turns out another day.
UPDATE- the frozen pan may have been a tiny step down from the original, but worked like a charm and was still delicious!!!

I love this recipe, and best of all, my husband loves it too! I make a few changes when I make it. Instead of cream of broccoli soup, I use cream of mushroom. I also add a small can of mushrooms to the onions to saute. What really gives mine some flavor is cooking up a whole pound of bacon, and crumbling it over top of the potatoes with the cheese! I make this often, and it tastes just as good for leftovers too!

So delicious! I'm giving it five stars for taste and how easy it is to make. I did use one cup of half & half instead of milk just because I thought it sounded extra good. And to make it more of a main dish I also cut up a store bought rotisserie chicken and layered it between the potatoes. This is an "even better the next day" dish.

This was great and i will use a base for scalloped potato going forward , i used cream of mushroom since i already had some and i halved the recipe so only 1 can and a handful of cheese , I used Mexican cheese blend , again using what i already had on hand
I used my mandolin to slice 1/4 inch 
Baked 1 hour with foil and taters were pretty done , baked without foil for 20 and broiled for 5-10 (gotta watch a broil no matter what ) 
When it comes to potato’s i agree that these can’t really be over cooked and you can’t rush them either. i always start potatoes 2 hours before they would need to be served. 
I served this with my corned beef for st Patrick’s day i know that’s not the norm but all my potatoes didn’t fit in my crock pot lol
I added a 16oz package of cubed fully cooked ham as a protein. Had to cook longer so potatoes were fully cooked. Great flavors!
Needs to be cooked at 400 degrees instead of 350 degrees—otherwise potatoes don’t get thoroughly cooked

Not a fan. Cooking time was way off! Recipe says 1 hour and 10 minutes. After the directed time, thin potato slices were still not cooked. I raised temp to 400 and cooked for an additional 45 minutes and potatoes were still a little chewy but the dish tasted good.
Followed the recipe right up to almost done; took the one reviewers suggestion of last 10 minutes uncovered, and sprinkled some paprika to melt in. End result: new family favorite.
Simple to make & absolutely DELICIOUS!
Pretty easy. I used a 3 lb. bag of red potatoes. My older son helped and he suggested adding a little bacon, which we may do next time. Either way DELICIOUS.

I made these as directed. I must say I was very disappointed. It definitely took a lot longer to cook and some of the potatoes were still not cooked through all the way (I used a mandolin to slice them so they were all cut the same thickness). I found them to be very bland tasting as well. And when I finally did take them out of the oven they were pretty soupy like.. like the sauce didn't really thicken up much.

My first time making scalloped potatoes not from a box. I had some ingredients I needed to use up so I didn’t follow the recipe exactly, but used it as a guide and would like to give it credit (thank you). I used russet potatoes, one can of cream of potato soup and one can of cheddar cheese soup. I added a head of broccoli chopped small, and the only cheese I had was jalapeño Jack. Very tasty! The only thing I regret is adding more salt as the soups are pretty salty, but overall it was a success!
Absolutely delicious! I did add some sour cream.
